newsitem.title: USA: Police hunt for killer of Bill Cosby's son.
newsitem.headline: Police hunt for killer of Bill Cosby's son.

text.p: Police searched on Friday for a lone gunman who killed the only son of comedian Bill Cosby as he changed a flat tire alongside a southern California freeway.

The murder of Ennis William Cosby early on Thursday in the chic Bel-Air neighbourhood sent shockwaves through Hollywood and sparked an outpouring of sympathy for his father -- one of the entertainment industry's most beloved figures.
The body of Cosby's 27-year-old son was found in a pool of blood beside his dark green Mercedes car by a woman who contacted police.

The identity of the woman, seen in television footage wearing a fur coat and high-heeled shoes, was being protected by police, since she was believed to be the only witness to the killing near an off-ramp on the usually busy San Diego Freeway.
But the Los Angeles Times cited sources as saying the woman was a friend of Ennis Cosby's and that he was on the way to meet her when he stopped to change a tire on a remote stretch of road.

Citing a highly placed source, the newspaper said 27-year-old Ennis Cosby had called her on his cellular phone in the early hours of Thursday to come to his aid and shine her car's headlights on his Mercedes convertible while he worked.
That was when she witnessed part of the attack.

The distraught woman, who was driving a Jaguar and wearing a fur coat, was questioned extensively by investigators. She described the gunman as a white male, and police said robbery was most likely the motive.

Cmdr. Tim McBride, a police spokesman, told the Times the woman was "freaking out" at the prospect of being pursued by reporters, fearing that the killer might retaliate against her. She was helping investigators put together a composite drawing of the suspect to be released to the public.

Bill Cosby and his wife Camille, who also have four daughters, were in New York when their son was killed. The taping of his CBS series "Cosby" was put on hold at a New York studio and Cosby, his wife and some family members, left their Manhattan home later on Thursday, their destination unknown.
Police claimed Cosby intended to fly to Los Angeles, but his Los Angeles-based publicist, David Brokaw, later denied that and said funeral arrangements had not been made.

Brokaw said Cosby called him from New York late on Thursday night. "He's bearing up as well as can be expected. But he's clearly distressed about what's happened," he said. "The family just wants some privacy right now."
"He was my hero," was all Cosby told reporters on Thursday as he ducked inside his home on Manhattan's Upper East Side.
Cosby appealed to police to do "anything possible" to catch the killer, said Cmdr. Tim McBride, a police spokesman.
Despite his personal tragedy Cosby planned to go ahead with plans to host an AIDS benefit at New York's Carnegie Hall next Wednesday, Brokaw said.
Hollywood meanwhile opened up with expressions of sympathy for one of the most popular personalities on television.
